name: Titanium dioxide
aliases: E171, titanium dioxide, dióxido de titanio, titanium white, CI Pigment White 6, anatase, rutile
what_is: An inorganic white mineral pigment historically used to whiten and brighten foods.
why_botia: BOTIA flags E171 because EFSA could not rule out genotoxicity and no longer considered it safe as a food additive. The EU removed its authorisation in 2022.
can_1: Identify E171 on scanned ingredient lists and issue a high-risk ban warning.
can_2: Say why E171 lost authorisation: genotoxicity could not be ruled out. Ovarian nanoparticle accumulation was not the established basis for the ban.
cannot_1: Identify whether a product purchased outside the EU still utilizes E171 unless indicated on the packaging.
cannot_2: Detect the exact proportion of nanoparticle-sized (less than 100 nm) titanium dioxide present in the additive.

sources.label: EFSA Scientific Opinion on the safety of titanium dioxide (E 171) as a food additive (2021)
